Sahra: Arabic and Somali variant of Sara/Sahar; Sahra is often linked to Arabic 'desert', while Sahar means 'dawn'. Origin partly uncertain.
Imraan: Arabic, a variant spelling of Imran, the Quranic name of the father of Maryam (Mary). Often interpreted as 'prosperity' or 'long-lived'.
Eduardo: Spanish and Portuguese form of Edward, from Old English ead 'wealth' and weard 'guardian'.
Haytham: Arabic, meaning 'young eagle' or 'young falcon'. Borne by the scholar Ibn al-Haytham.
Moustapha: French spelling of Arabic Mustafa, meaning 'the chosen one'. An epithet of the Prophet Muhammad.
Lidia: Latinised form of Lydia, from the ancient region of Lydia in Anatolia; also used in Spanish, Italian and Polish. Mentioned in the New Testament.
Elyssa: Modern variant of Elissa or Alyssa. Elissa is a name of Dido of Carthage; Alyssa is linked to the alyssum flower. Origin uncertain.
Andrés: Spanish form of Andrew, from Greek andreios 'manly, brave'.
Hebe: Greek, from hebe 'youth'. The goddess of youth in Greek mythology.
Derek: English form of Dutch Diederik (Theodoric), from Germanic theud 'people' and ric 'ruler'.
Arthus: French variant of Arthur, a Celtic name of uncertain meaning, possibly 'bear' (Welsh arth). Linked to the legendary King Arthur.
Kiki: Short pet name used in many languages, often from names like Christine or Kristina. Also Japanese kiki 'happiness' in some uses.
Ambroise: French form of Ambrose, from Greek ambrosios 'immortal'. Borne by Saint Ambrose of Milan.
Anaë: Breton and French form of Anna, from Hebrew Channah 'grace, favour'. Possibly also a Breton variant of Anaïs.
Gitty: Yiddish, from Gitl, meaning 'good'. Used mainly in Jewish communities.
Viola: Latin for the violet flower. Used in Italian and English; a Shakespearean heroine in Twelfth Night.
Zeinab: Arabic, a variant of Zaynab, from a fragrant tree, or 'father's jewel'. Name of the Prophet's daughter.
Lissandro: Probably a modern variant of Lisandro or Alessandro, from Greek 'defender of men'. Lysander means 'liberator'.
Idil: Turkish, from Idyll, meaning 'idyll' or 'pastoral peace'. Also spelled Idil in Turkey.
Larisa: Greek, from the city Larissa in Thessaly, possibly meaning 'citadel'. Common in Slavic and Romanian use.
Malaika: Swahili and Arabic-derived word for 'angels'. Used as a girls' name in East Africa.
Lexa: Short form of Alexandra, from Greek 'defender of men'. Also used as an independent modern name.
Nunzio: Italian, from Latin nuntius 'messenger'. Often a short form of Annunziato, 'the announced one'.
Samuele: Italian form of Samuel, from Hebrew Shemu'el, usually explained as 'God has heard' or 'name of God'.
Aure: French short form of Aurélie or Aurore, from Latin aurum 'gold' or aurora 'dawn'. Origin partly uncertain.
Hamid: Arabic, meaning 'praiseworthy' or 'thankful'. Related to Muhammad and Ahmad.
Majid: Arabic, meaning 'glorious' or 'noble'. One of the attributes of God in Islam.
Toma: Slavic, Romanian and Georgian form of Thomas, from Aramaic ta'oma 'twin'.
Nasr: Arabic, meaning 'victory' or 'help'. Also the Arabic word for eagle in related forms.
Ella-Noor: Compound of Ella, a Germanic short name meaning 'all' or related to Eleanor, and Arabic Noor 'light'.
Biagio: Italian form of Blaise, from Latin Blasius, probably from blaesus 'lisping' or 'stuttering'. Saint Blaise is a martyr.
Yumi: Japanese, with meanings depending on the kanji, such as 'beautiful' or 'bow'.
Liandro: Probably a modern variant of Leandro, the Spanish and Portuguese form of Leander, from Greek 'lion man'.
Melyna: Modern variant of Melina, from Greek meli 'honey' or from names ending in -melina. Origin uncertain.
Sulaiman: Arabic form of Solomon, from Hebrew Shlomo, related to shalom 'peace'.
Rares: Romanian, from Latin rarus via Romanian rar 'rare'. Popular in Romania, sometimes explained as a form of Rareș.
Reina: Spanish for 'queen', from Latin regina. Also a Japanese name with varied meanings.
Amirah: Arabic, feminine of Amir, meaning 'princess' or 'commander'.
Ilia: Variant of Elijah or Ilya, from Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'. Also used in Greek and Russian contexts.
Safiatou: West African French spelling of Arabic Safiyyah, meaning 'pure' or 'chosen friend'.
Aurel: Romanian and German form of Latin Aurelius, from aureus 'golden'.
Aysel: Turkish, from ay 'moon' and sel 'flood', or 'moonlight'. Also used in Azerbaijan.
Finley: Scottish and Irish, from Gaelic Fionnlagh, meaning 'fair hero' or 'fair warrior'.
Mit: Probably a short form of Mitchell or a Thai or Hindi name meaning 'friend' (mitra). Origin uncertain.
Safiyah: Arabic, meaning 'pure' or 'sincere friend'. A wife of the Prophet Muhammad.
Sebastián: Spanish form of Sebastian, from Greek sebastos 'venerable', denoting a person from Sebaste.
Cil: Probably a short form of Cillian, an Irish name possibly meaning 'church' or 'strife'. Origin uncertain.
Timeea: Romanian form of Timaia or Timea; Timea is Hungarian, from Greek timios 'honoured, precious'.
Gia: Short form of Italian Gianna or Giovanna, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'. Also Georgian Gia, a form of George.
Aiza: Arabic and Urdu name, possibly meaning 'honoured' or 'powerful'. Origin uncertain.
María: Spanish form of Mary, from Hebrew Miryam, of uncertain meaning, possibly 'beloved' or 'wished-for child'.
Subhan: Arabic, meaning 'glory' or 'glorified'. Often part of the phrase Subhan Allah.
Amaliya: Slavic and Arabic-influenced form of Amalia, from Germanic amal 'work'. Also related to Arabic amal 'hope'.
Atilio: Spanish and Italian form of Latin Attilius, a Roman family name, possibly from Atta 'father'.
Rimas: Lithuanian male name, possibly from rimtas 'serious, calm'. Also used as Arabic Rima 'white antelope'. Origin uncertain.
Nara: Japanese place name (Nara city), also Korean 'country', and Sanskrit-related uses. Meaning depends on the culture.
Daiana: Romanian and Spanish form of Diana, the Roman goddess of the moon and hunting; from Latin 'divine'.
Assile: Probably a variant of Arabic Asil or Aseel, meaning 'authentic' or 'of noble origin'. Origin uncertain.
Izao: Origin uncertain; possibly a modern coined name or of Portuguese or Asian origin.
Abubakr: Arabic, Abu Bakr 'father of the young camel'. Name of the first caliph of Islam.
Jalia: Arabic Jalila or Jaliyah variant, meaning 'exalted' or 'clear'. Also Ugandan use. Origin uncertain.
Sudais: Arabic, from sudus 'sixth'. A surname of the imam Abdul Rahman al-Sudais.
Fateh: Arabic, Persian and Punjabi name meaning 'conqueror' or 'victory'.
Isaaq: Variant of Isaac, from Hebrew Yitzchak 'he will laugh'. Also the name of a Somali clan.
Elira: Albanian, from elirë 'free'; also used as 'free woman'.
Uras: Turkish, meaning 'strong' or 'courageous'. Also Sardinian place name. Origin partly uncertain.
Larien: Probably a modern or fantasy name, possibly Tolkien-inspired. Origin uncertain.
Zohan: Probably a variant of Zohar or Zoan; Zohar is Hebrew 'radiance'. Also popularised by a film. Origin uncertain.
Mélyo: Modern French coined name, possibly from Mélio or Mélissa-type names. Origin uncertain.
Idalia: Greek, from the Cypriot city Idalion, linked to Aphrodite. Used in Spanish and English.
Oussaïd: Arabic, from Usaid or Asid, meaning 'little lion'. French North African spelling.
Mariia: Ukrainian and Russian transliteration of Maria, from Hebrew Miryam, meaning uncertain.
Joren: Dutch and Flemish short form, likely a variant of Joran, itself a Dutch form of George or Jordan. Origin partly uncertain.
Hannelore: German, a compound of Hanne (from Johanna) and Lore (from Eleonore or Laura). Means 'God is gracious'.
Chelsea: English, from the London district, from Old English 'landing place for chalk'.
Tatiana: Russian and Latin, from the Roman family name Tatius. Borne by Saint Tatiana of Rome.
Kyra: Greek feminine of Kyros, meaning 'lady' or 'mistress'. Also linked to Persian Cyrus.
Tijs: Dutch short form of Matthijs, the Dutch form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Sylvain: French, from Latin Silvanus, 'of the forest'. Silvanus was the Roman god of woods.
Johan: Scandinavian and Dutch form of John, from Hebrew Yochanan 'God is gracious'.
Rob: Short form of Robert, from Germanic hrod 'fame' and beraht 'bright'.
Thiméo: Modern French form of Timéo or Timothée, from Greek timotheos 'honouring God'. Probably influenced by Théo.
Hatice: Turkish form of Arabic Khadija, 'premature child'. Name of the Prophet's first wife.
Vadim: Slavic, from Old Russian vaditi 'to rule'. Popular in Russia and Ukraine. Origin partly uncertain.
Kylie: Australian Aboriginal, probably 'boomerang', or a modern English form of Kyle meaning 'strait'. Origin debated.
Carl: Germanic and Scandinavian form of Charles, from karl 'free man'.
Emme: Probably a variant of Emma, from Germanic ermen 'whole' or 'universal'.
Célya: Modern French variant of Célia or Célie, from Latin Caelia, 'heavenly'. Probably influenced by Célia.
Antonino: Italian diminutive of Antonio, from Latin Antonius, a Roman family name of uncertain meaning.
Lancelot: French, the knight of Arthurian legend. Possibly from Lance with a diminutive suffix. Origin uncertain.
José: Spanish, Portuguese and French form of Joseph, from Hebrew 'God will add'.
Kas: Dutch short form of Casper or Cas, from Persian 'treasurer'. Also used as an independent name.
Hava: Hebrew and Turkish form of Eve, from Hebrew chavah 'life'. In Turkish, hava means 'air'.
Souhail: Arabic Suhail, the name of the star Canopus. Often explained as 'smooth' or 'easy'.
Paco: Spanish pet form of Francisco, from Latin Franciscus 'Frenchman' or 'free man'.
Maëlyne: Modern French name, probably a blend of Maëlle and Eline. Maël is Breton for 'prince'.
Cristian: Spanish, Italian and Romanian form of Christian, from Latin christianus 'follower of Christ'.
Elli: Finnish and Greek short form of Eleni or Eleonora. Also a Finnish pet form of Eleonora.
Mick: Short form of Michael, from Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Niko: Short form of Nikolaus or Nikolas, from Greek 'victory of the people'.
Magdalena: From Mary Magdalene, 'woman of Magdala'. Magdala is a town in Galilee, from Hebrew migdal 'tower'.
Yan: Chinese 'swallow' or other meanings. In Europe, also a form of Jan, from John 'God is gracious'.
Kayra: Turkish, meaning 'favour' or 'goodness'. Also used as a masculine name.
Ramses: Egyptian, from Ra-messu 'born of Ra'. The name of several pharaohs.
Paulin: French form of Latin Paulinus, a diminutive of Paulus 'small, humble'.
Virgil: English form of Latin Vergilius, a Roman family name of uncertain meaning. Borne by the poet of the Aeneid.
Edmond: French form of Edmund, from Old English ead 'wealth' and mund 'protection'.
Karla: Feminine form of Karl, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Ole: Scandinavian form of Olaf, from Old Norse 'ancestor's descendant'. Also used in Frisian regions.
Toni: Short form of Anthony or Antonia. Antonius is a Roman family name of uncertain meaning.
Kornelia: Feminine form of Cornelius, from the Roman family name possibly from cornu 'horn'.
Akim: Russian form of Joachim, from Hebrew 'God will establish'. Also an Arabic and Ghanaian name.
Runa: Scandinavian, from Old Norse rún 'secret, rune'. Also Japanese or Bengali uses.
Kenaya: Modern coined name, possibly from Kenya or Hebrew-style 'kena'. Origin uncertain.
Jaylinn: Modern American coined name, from Jay and the suffix -lynn. No traditional meaning.
Mariano: Spanish and Italian, from Latin Marianus, 'belonging to Marius' or devoted to Mary.
Holly: English, from the holly plant, traditionally associated with Christmas.
Zyan: Modern coined name, perhaps a variant of Zayn or Ziyan. Origin uncertain.
Marcelin: French form of Marcellinus, a diminutive of Marcellus, itself derived from Marcus, perhaps 'warlike'.
Achil: Probably a variant of Achille, from Greek Achilleus, of uncertain meaning. Borne by the Greek hero.
Dov: Hebrew, meaning 'bear'. Also used as a short form of Dovid.
Macéo: Modern French name, probably a variant of Marceau or Maceo, a Spanish surname perhaps from Matthew.
Sofiya: Slavic and Central Asian form of Sophia, from Greek sophia 'wisdom'.
Eliya: Variant of Elijah, from Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'. Also used for girls.
Soulaiman: French spelling of Arabic Sulayman, the form of Solomon, related to Hebrew shalom 'peace'.
Haroune: French spelling of Arabic Harun, the form of Aaron. Meaning uncertain, perhaps 'mountain of strength'.
Cassian: From Latin Cassianus, 'belonging to Cassius'. Borne by several early saints.
Amaia: Basque, from a place name meaning 'the end' or 'the beginning'. Common in the Basque Country.
Dawoed: Dutch and Arabic spelling of David or Dawud, from Hebrew 'beloved'.
Lizet: Spanish and French variant of Lizette or Lisette, a diminutive of Elisabeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Bea: Short form of Beatrix or Beatrice, from Latin 'she who brings happiness'.
Tesnime: Arabic Tasnim, a fountain in paradise in the Quran. Also read as 'raised high'.
Zélya: Modern French variant of Zélie or Zelia, from Greek zelos 'zeal'. Origin partly uncertain.
Arin: Possibly Hebrew 'mountain' or Armenian and Persian, with 'peaceful'. Meaning varies by culture; origin uncertain.
Aylina: Modern name, probably from Turkish ay 'moon' with the suffix -lina, or a blend of Aylin. Origin uncertain.
Maliya: Probably a variant of Malia or Maliyah, itself a Hawaiian form of Maria or Arabic 'wealthy'. Origin uncertain.
Artémis: French form of Artemis, the Greek goddess of the hunt. Meaning uncertain, possibly 'safe' or 'butcher'.
Ohana: Hawaiian, meaning 'family'. Popularised by the film Lilo and Stitch.
Suzette: French diminutive of Suzanne, from Hebrew shoshana 'lily'.
Lowis: Dutch variant of Lodewijk or Louis, from Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Lyno: Modern French coined name, possibly from Lino or Lyonel. Origin uncertain.
Keyna: Modern variant of Keyna or Kenya, possibly from the country. Also Welsh saint Ceinwen/Keyne. Origin uncertain.
Maëlyo: Modern French coined name, probably a variant of Maël with -o ending. Maël is Breton 'prince'.
Ezequiel: Spanish form of Ezekiel, from Hebrew 'God strengthens'.
Soann: Breton variant of Joanne or Soan, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'. Origin uncertain.
Larin: Probably a variant of Laren or Lorin, from Laurentius. Also a Russian surname. Origin uncertain.
Rafa: Short form of Rafael, from Hebrew 'God has healed'.
Lyon: French city name, from Latin Lugdunum, 'fort of the god Lugus'. Also a variant of Leon.
Naé: Probably a French form of Noé (Noah) or Nae, Hebrew 'rest'. Origin uncertain.
Manissa: Probably a modern variant of Manisha, Sanskrit 'wisdom, intellect'. Origin uncertain.
Safiyyah: Arabic, meaning 'pure' or 'chosen friend'. A wife of Muhammad.
Thylio: Modern French coined name, perhaps from Thilo or Tilio. Origin uncertain.
Brielle: French diminutive of Gabrielle, meaning 'God is my strength'.
Liyanah: Arabic, meaning 'soft' or 'tender'. A variant of Lina or Liyana.
Hilona: Probably a variant of Hilone or Hylona, possibly from Greek 'wooded'. Origin uncertain.
Rosalía: Spanish form of Rosalia, from Latin rosa 'rose'. Borne by Saint Rosalia of Palermo.
Novi: Probably from Slavic or Latin novus 'new'. Also an Indonesian name. Origin uncertain.
Aleya: Probably a variant of Aliyah or Aleia, from Arabic 'exalted'. Origin partly uncertain.
Monti: Probably a short form of Montgomery or Montague, or from Italian monte 'mountain'. Origin uncertain.
Mavie: Modern French coined name, possibly from 'ma vie' ('my life'). Probably a recent invention.
Ostap: Ukrainian form of Eustace, from Greek 'fruitful' or 'stable'.
Stien: Dutch short form of Christine or Justine. From Latin 'Christian' or 'just'.
Erin: Irish, from Éirinn, poetic name for Ireland, meaning 'western island'.
Loredana: Italian, probably from the Venetian surname Loredan, which derives from Loreo. Popularised by a 20th-century singer.
Renaud: French form of Reynold, from Germanic ragin 'counsel' and wald 'rule'.
Kaoutar: Arabic Kawthar, 'abundance'. A river in Paradise in the Quran.
Evelyne: French form of Evelyn, from Norman Aveline, perhaps from a Germanic name 'desired'. Also a hazel nut name.
Sabrine: French variant of Sabrina, the Latin name of the River Severn. Also used as Arabic Sabrin.
Noéline: French feminine of Noël, from Latin natalis 'birthday', meaning Christmas.
Yacine: Arabic Yasin, a name for the Prophet. A Quranic letter combination meaning uncertain.
Prince: English, from Latin princeps 'first, chief', denoting the son of a king.
Leandra: Feminine of Leander, from Greek 'lion man'.
Vinn: Probably a short form of Vincent or Vinny, from Latin vincere 'to conquer'. Origin uncertain.
Dalya: Hebrew 'branch' or 'vine branch', or Arabic 'grape vine'. A modern name in both cultures.
Eliah: Variant of Elijah, from Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Ikhlas: Arabic, meaning 'sincerity'. The title of the 112th chapter of the Quran.
Mélusine: French, from medieval legend of a water spirit. Possibly from Latin 'Melusina', meaning uncertain.
Solan: Probably from Latin sol 'sun' or a Norse and French surname. Also a Spanish place name. Origin uncertain.
Siënna: Variant of Sienna, from the Italian city and the brownish pigment, terra di Siena.
Xem: Probably a modern or foreign short name; origin uncertain. Possibly Vietnamese or a variant of Xem.
